ip_top_stories.title: GEMA Wins Against Suno: Europe's First AI Music Ruling — Here's What's Behind It
ip_top_stories.summary: A German court has ruled in favour of music rights organisation GEMA against AI music platform Suno, finding that Suno's AI training practices infringed copyright. The case is being widely described as Europe's first major AI music copyright ruling, rejecting Suno's fair use-style defence. The decision has significant implications for how AI companies may use copyrighted music in training datasets.

ip_top_stories.title: Princeton University Press Partners with Cashmere on AI Licensing [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: Princeton University Press has announced a licensing partnership with Cashmere, an AI licensing platform, to enable authorised use of its content for AI training. The deal represents a growing trend of academic publishers seeking structured licensing arrangements rather than litigation as a response to AI training on copyrighted works.

ip_top_stories.title: Midjourney Copied Thousands of Car Photos to Train AI, Suit Says
ip_top_stories.summary: A new lawsuit alleges that AI image generator Midjourney used thousands of copyrighted car photographs without authorisation to train its AI model. The case adds to the growing body of litigation targeting AI companies over their training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Reddit's DMCA Claims Against Perplexity, SerpApi Survive AI Scraping Challenge
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has allowed Reddit's DMCA claims against AI search company Perplexity and scraping service SerpApi to proceed, under a broad reading of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. The ruling is significant for how DMCA protections may apply to AI-driven web scraping at scale.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC's OpenAI-ANI Ruling: What It Means for AI, Copyright and Publishers in India | Hindustan Times
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court's ruling in the ANI versus OpenAI case is analysed for its implications for AI copyright law and publishers in India. The piece examines how the court's findings on AI training and news content could shape future policy and litigation across the publishing sector.

ip_further_links.title: AI Firms Shred Rare Books Post-Digitization
ip_further_links.summary: Reports have emerged that AI companies have been destroying rare physical books after digitising them for AI training purposes, raising serious concerns about preservation ethics and copyright compliance.

ip_further_links.title: Investors Blast Nvidia Over Avalanche of AI Copyright Suits
ip_further_links.summary: Nvidia shareholders have raised concerns about the company's exposure to the growing wave of AI copyright litigation, questioning how the firm is managing legal risk.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI's EU AI Act Statement Skips Training Data: Copyright Gap Activates Sunday
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of OpenAI's EU AI Act compliance statement reveals it omits detail on training data practices, raising concerns about a copyright transparency gap as new obligations came into force.

ip_further_links.title: From 'Daddy Cool' to the Docket: How Latham & Quinn Emanuel Are Testing AI Music in Court
ip_further_links.summary: A look at how major law firms Latham & Watkins and Quinn Emanuel are shaping legal strategy around the Suno AI music copyright cases and what arguments are being tested in court.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright in AI Era: Deeper Judicial, Legislative Scrutiny Is Needed
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece argues that existing copyright frameworks are insufficient to address AI-related infringement and calls for more rigorous judicial and legislative engagement with the issue.

ip_further_links.title: GCC Bans AI-Generated Code Over GPL Copyright Fears
ip_further_links.summary: The GNU Compiler Collection project has banned AI-generated code contributions amid concerns that such code could infringe GPL licence terms and introduce unresolved copyright complications.

ip_further_links.title: Research Rejuvenated: ANI v. OpenAI and the DPDPA
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the Indian ANI versus OpenAI copyright case examines its intersection with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act and the implications for AI training on news content.

ip_further_links.title: Sci-fi Authors Scalzi and Stross Decry AI's Dystopian Impact on Their Craft
ip_further_links.summary: Prominent science fiction authors John Scalzi and Charles Stross have spoken out against AI's use of their work without consent, describing its impact on professional authorship as deeply damaging.

ip_further_links.title: Actor Shruti Haasan Moves Bombay High Court Over AI Deepfakes, Personality Rights Violations
ip_further_links.summary: Indian actor Shruti Haasan has filed a petition in the Bombay High Court seeking protection against unauthorised AI deepfakes and violations of her personality rights.

ip_further_links.title: From Talking Point to Contractual Concern: Hewitt Glass' Julian Hewitt and Rob Glass Discuss AI
ip_further_links.summary: Legal practitioners Julian Hewitt and Rob Glass discuss how AI intellectual property issues are increasingly appearing in commercial contracts and what legal professionals need to consider.
